activities.anchor: whose 76-second half-life suits heart perfusion PET
activities.caption: file each isotope by its production route
activities.name: rphRouteSort

config.prompt: Three routes make an atom glow — file each isotope:

items.label: molybdenum-99 — a fission fragment of split uranium
iodine-131 — a neutron-rich beta emitter for therapy
fluorine-18 — knocked proton-rich out of oxygen-18 water
technetium-99m — the daughter milked overnight from a column
gallium-68 — grown from germanium-68 for neuroendocrine imaging

config.why: The route fixes the decay behaviour: reactors make neutron-rich beta emitters, accelerators make proton-rich positron emitters, generators convert a weekly shipment into a daily supply.

activities.anchor: long enough to prepare, inject and image over several hours
activities.caption: true or false — reading half-lives
activities.name: rphHalfLifeJudge

statements.s: An isotope's half-life measures how dangerous it is.
statements.why: Half-life is a clock, not a hazard dial — short means the dose ends quickly but leaves little time to work.

statements.s: There is a single best isotope for all of nuclear medicine.
statements.why: Each half-life is a trade: short suits imaging, long suits therapy — the job picks the isotope.

statements.s: A long half-life always images better.
statements.why: Long suits therapy but complicates imaging — the patient's dose lingers.

statements.s: Technetium-99m's six hours are valued as a compromise.
statements.why: A deliberate sweet spot — and why it runs in roughly four out of five diagnostic studies worldwide.

activities.anchor: minutes later the dose is ready to assay
activities.caption: sequence the hot lab's morning
activities.name: rphHotLabOrder

config.prompt: The daily rhythm, in working order:
items: Elute the generator — wash saline through the column and collect the overnight daughter
Compound the kit — add the eluate to the freeze-dried vial and heat where required
Draw the dose and measure it in the calibrator, logged against the prescription
Release only when radiochemical purity passes — unbound activity would fog the scan
config.why: Every aliquot and elution then lands in decay-corrected logbooks regulators can audit — the rhythm is production line, not improvisation.

activities.anchor: the free isotope would streak into the thyroid and stomach and fog the image
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the purity note
activities.name: rphPuritySpot

config.prompt: One line of this hot-lab note is wrong — click it:
lines: Kit compounding runs under the same aseptic discipline as any intravenous preparation.
The dose calibrator is a precision ionisation chamber; its reading is logged against the prescription.
Thin-layer chromatography checks radiochemical purity before release.
Free pertechnetate in a vial is harmless — it images the same target as the bound courier.
Every elution and assay is written into decay-corrected logbooks regulators can audit.
config.correction: Unbound activity localises to organs the courier never chose and degrades the study — a vial below the release threshold is discarded.
config.why: Purity gates both image quality and the patient's dose — that is why 97 percent bound passes and less does not.

activities.anchor: adds contamination control to the classic trio
activities.caption: drag between sealed-source and unsealed-source discipline
activities.name: rphAlaraCompare

config.prompt: Drag across the protection problem — same ALARA, two source types:

before.label: the classic trio
before.text: Minimise time near the source, maximise distance, use shielding — the whole discipline for a source that stays where you put it.

after.label: the unsealed twist
after.text: The material can spill, spread and stick: absorbent bench covers, dedicated pipettes, wipe tests on surfaces, disciplined monitoring of hands and clothing — plus tungsten or lead around everything from generator to syringe.

config.why: Hot-lab protection is the classic trio plus a fourth discipline — because an unsealed source travels on dust, gloves and benches.

activities.anchor: comparable to or smaller than a few months of natural background
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the seatmate question
activities.name: rphPatientPredict

config.q: A patient leaves the department an hour after a diagnostic tracer dose. The dose to the person seated next to them on the bus is best described as…
choices: Like standing beside an X-ray machine all day
Dangerous until the tracer is fully excreted
Tiny — diagnostic doses run at or below a few months of natural background
Zero, because the tracer is gone at injection
config.why: The activity is tiny and the half-life short; historic 'no hugging' advice has largely relaxed — sensible hygiene simply speeds the exit of a tracer the body is already clearing.

activities.anchor: the reticuloendothelial system drawn in light
activities.caption: pair each mechanism with its tracer
activities.name: rphLocaliseMatch

config.prompt: Six localisation mechanisms, five shown — pair each with its example:

pairs.right: iodide pumped into thyroid cells at tens of times its blood concentration
MAA particles too wide for lung capillaries lodge in the pulmonary bed
Kupffer cells swallow sulphur colloid — liver, spleen and marrow light up
FDG-6-phosphate is a dead end the cell cannot process or export
sestamibi seeps into heart muscle and sticks to mitochondria

config.why: A tracer cannot be forced anywhere — the designer exploits a mechanism the body already runs, which is what any given scan can and cannot see.

config.root: A PET scan shows one bright spot. Walk the reading a radiologist actually runs.

start.text: What does brightness mean, first of all?

choices.label: It is cancer until proven otherwise
Activity — the tracer concentrated where metabolism runs

backwards.text: That is exactly backwards: uptake means activity — healing, filtering, metabolising — and both bright and dark are findings.

function.text: But FDG does not know cancer from inflammation — both burn glucose. What completes the read?

choices.label: Correlate against anatomy from a fused CT and the patient's history
Report the bright spot as malignancy

solo.text: Uptake is not specific to disease — the tracer pattern is read against anatomy and history, never alone.

done.text: Hot means activity, cold means the tracer never arrived, and neither is specific to disease without anatomy and history alongside.

config.why: The diagnostic skill is separating the physiology that lights up from the pathology that also lights up — the black holes matter just as much.
